players.product: PCBs for DDR5 server memory modules (R-DIMM / U-DIMM / SO-DIMM), SSDs and back-end test equipment

quarterly_data.signal: H1 2026 results (DART half-year report filed 08-14-2026, consolidated): revenue KRW 164,078,081,926 vs KRW 117,042,933,586 in H1 2025; gross profit KRW 31,352,296,680; operating profit KRW 23,491,381,156 vs KRW 8,730,563,273; net income KRW 19,226,892,812 vs KRW 5,387,214,165. Q2 alone: revenue KRW 88,243,337,682 vs KRW 64,053,168,694; operating profit KRW 12,772,973,583 vs KRW 6,856,979,236; net income KRW 10,758,976,869. 100% of revenue is PCBs (SSD, memory module and new business incl. back-end test-equipment PCBs); exports KRW 147,562,921 thousand = 89.9% of revenue (domestic 10.1%). Average selling price KRW 1,361,056 per m2 in H1 2026 vs KRW 1,095,566 in 2025 and KRW 843,160 in 2024. Vietnam subsidiary TLB VINA: H1 revenue KRW 27,688,007 thousand vs KRW 3,846,698 thousand in H1 2025, net income KRW 836,277 thousand vs a KRW 3,341,238 thousand loss.

Order book (DART half-year report filed 08-14-2026): PCB orders received 2026-01-01 to 2026-06-30 totalled KRW 2,959 x 100M, of which KRW 1,641 x 100M was delivered, leaving an order backlog of KRW 1,318 x 100M.
quarterly_data.figure: Orders KRW 2,959 x 100M; delivered 1,641; backlog KRW 1,318 x 100M at 06-30-2026

quarterly_data.signal: Capacity, utilisation and capex (DART half-year report filed 08-14-2026): H1 2026 PCB capacity 174,000 m2 (29,000 m2 per month) vs 348,000 m2 per year in 2022-2025; production 123,187 m2; UTILISATION 70.80% vs 69.75% in 2025, 62.71% in 2024 and 81.68% in 2022. H1 PP&E purchases KRW 20,173,016,786 vs KRW 6,580,658,315 in H1 2025; construction-in-progress KRW 37,789,777,055 (vs KRW 26,055,777,937 at 2025-12-31). The company has a land purchase contract in the Yongin Semiconductor Cluster industrial complex to build a new factory: KRW 7,009,880,000 in total, paid in instalments through 2027, KRW 6,308,892,000 paid so far. The filing says no other investment is in progress and further plans will be disclosed once approved by the board. Input costs rose: gold potassium cyanide (PGC) KRW 152,044/g vs KRW 109,445 in 2025, CCL KRW 6,869/panel vs 6,238, copper foil KRW 1,183/sheet vs 983.
quarterly_data.figure: Utilisation 70.80% (123,187 of 174,000 m2); H1 capex KRW 20,173,016,786; Yongin cluster factory land KRW 7,009,880,000

quarterly_data.signal: Products and roadmap (DART half-year report filed 08-14-2026): the company says it is participating in SOCAMM (LPDDR-based detachable AI-server memory module) development with major global semiconductor and memory makers and is responding to mass production this year; it expects CXL memory-expansion modules and high-speed AI-server PCBs to expand. High-value products using the BVH (blind via hole) process for DDR5 high-end servers have raised their share of revenue every quarter since Q1 2025, and the filing says BVH-based DDR5 server orders contributed to 2025 revenue growth. Other positioning: e-SSD share of SSD PCBs rising with AI demand; EDSFF SSD PCB development; Build-up / thin-CCL capability for DDR6; 1-5 layer skip-via test and development completed (the company claims no one else applies it); AS9100 and ISO27001 obtained in 2025 for aerospace / defence. R&D spend KRW 5,578,990 thousand (3.4% of revenue).
quarterly_data.figure: SOCAMM mass-production response in 2026; BVH DDR5 server PCB share rising each quarter since Q1 2025

quarterly_data.signal: Supplier Doosan Corporation (Doosan Electronics): H1 2026 raw-material purchases per the DART half-year report - CCL KRW 17,406,615,992 (28% of purchases) and prepreg KRW 8,208,112,631 (13%) mainly from Doosan Electronics; copper foil KRW 1,955,482,210 (3%) from Kyungdong Materials and others; gold potassium cyanide (PGC) KRW 21,286,140,000 (35%) from Heesung Catalysts. Total purchases KRW 61,157,488,255.
quarterly_data.figure: CCL KRW 17,406,615,992 (28%) + prepreg KRW 8,208,112,631 (13%) from Doosan Electronics; PGC KRW 21,286,140,000 (35%)

contracts.signal: DART half-year report names Samsung Electronics among TLB's main customers (with SK Hynix and Micron); a dedicated sales group 2 manages Samsung domestic and overseas accounts. The filing recalls that TLB built Korea's first SSD PCB mass-production system and supplied high-end SSD PCBs to Samsung for Apple MacBook Air.
DART half-year report names SK Hynix among TLB's main customers; a dedicated sales group 1 manages SK Hynix domestic and overseas accounts and new semiconductor-test business customers.
DART half-year report names Micron (US) among TLB's main customers alongside Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix; exports were 89.9% of H1 2026 revenue.
